parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing criminal exposure: no trans-specific offence, no facility or border restriction, no documented targeting of visitors. Structural signals point to a functioning rule-of-law state within a regional equality framework, with hate-speech/hate-crime law covering gender identity and conversion practices banned. The operative weaknesses are enforcement-side: documented police failures to establish hate motives, clergy incitement unprosecuted, and inconsistent enforcement — thin or partial recourse for a visitor facing street hostility. Pending LGR law and absent anti-discrimination ground are resident-facing gaps that do not reach visitors. Minors: no documented age-specific traveller exposure. Extrapolating from the mixed record: reduced risk, above enforcement-failure mid-cases but below jurisdictions with documented working remedies.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented friction for trans visitors at borders; passport marker practice not addressed.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor relies on home-issued documents; no domestic regime touches them.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: Prison guards received two-day LGBTI+ training (2023) after ombudsman complaints — resident-facing climate signal.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented custody-placement rule reaching visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility bans or birth-sex placement rules documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Regional-union equality directives shape the framework.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Divided island: one part runs its own recognition including non-binary identities; no visitor-facing divergence documented.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors; health-care coverage reported (2017) though framework called fragmented.
care_services.interaction: Visitors use travel-time prescriptions; no documented refusal cases.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Inconsistent enforcement: 2019 capital attacks drew no established hate motive or police action; clergy incitement sometimes unprosecuted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Article 99 hate-speech offence covers gender identity (fines raised 2024); prejudice as aggravating factor.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Recourse exists on paper but is unreliable in practice.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented as reaching visiting families.
minors_guardians.interaction: Adoption limited to heterosexual couples — resident-facing only.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two documented capital incidents (2019) with police inaction; many LGBTI people do not report violence — underreporting noted.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Criminal incitement and hate-crime law; support line operates daily.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police failure to act is the operative weakness.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: document-belief practice at entry, current status of LGR bill, unreconciled discrimination-coverage claims.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Accepted all SOGIESC review recommendations (2019); regional commission monitoring 2020/2024.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin recourse where enforcement lapses; no documented remedy failure against visitors.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.55-B, discretion and inconsistent official responses create uncertainty, but this dossier lacks any documented visitor screening, secondary-inspection, or denial-of-entry pattern; worst documented features are police inaction after violence, not border exposure — materially above 0.55-B.

0.65-D shows state detention of a visitor later remedied; here no visitor detention is documented, but police failures on hate crimes are comparable state shortfalls. Between 0.65-D and lower-0.75: no visitor-specific incident, but recourse is thinner.

0.75-D documents working prosecution of attackers with imperfect night-life response; this dossier's documented pattern is enforcement failure rather than success. Slightly below 0.75-D on recourse, but the broader legal framework (hate-speech offence, conversion ban, regional equality machinery) matches that tier.

Unlike 0.35-B's systematic police profiling of trans visitors, no targeting of trans people by police is documented here; criminalisation is absent and hate-crime law exists — categorically above the High Risk band.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime presents no universal-exposure measure: no facility restriction, document regime, or criminal offence reaches a trans visitor. The heaviest documented feature is tier-3 — societal hostility expressed as hate crimes met with inconsistent police response and unprosecuted incitement — partially mitigated by genuine legal protections (gender-identity hate-speech offence with raised fines, aggravating-factor rule, conversion-practices ban) and regional-union oversight. Resident-facing gaps (pending LGR, absent anti-discrimination ground, marriage/adoption limits) do not touch visitors. Net: reduced risk with a real enforcement-recourse deduction, sitting at the lower edge of the Reduced band.
